pending_commit.commit_message: BACKPORT: drm/i915: Nuke legacy flip queueing code Just a very minimal patch to nuke that code. Lots of the flip interrupt handling stuff is still around. Cc: Maarten Lankhorst <maarten.lankhorst@linux.intel.com> Cc: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Reviewed-by: Maarten Lankhorst <maarten.lankhorst@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@intel.com> Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20170719125502.25696-2-daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch (cherry picked from commit afa8ce5b3080146940f0fbe3363a139e777c46ac) from v4.14-rc1 Signed-off-by: Tarun Vyas <tarun.vyas@intel.com> BUG=b:70920211, b:109823283 TEST=No *Potential atomic update error* in dmesg with external display connected and browser opened and cursor blinking in address bar for PSR entry-exit TEST=No other regressions on KBL/APL/BYT based devices Conflicts: drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c [Tarun: We have ctx delta b/c of the following commits, but all of that is a don't care since this code is affirmatively dead and should be deleted regardless.] ["73dec95 drm/i915: Emit to ringbuffer directly"] ["e642c85 drm/i915: Remove superfluous i915_add_request_no_flush() helper"] Change-Id: Ic622754610ea7d047bdd58c840cd88edffe552d8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1135373 Commit-Ready: Nathan Ciobanu <nathan.d.ciobanu@intel.com> Tested-by: Casey G Bowman <casey.g.bowman@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nathan Ciobanu <nathan.d.ciobanu@intel.com>

BACKPORT: drm/i915: Pass the crtc state explicitly to intel_pipe_update_start/end() Pass the appropriate new crtc state explicitly to intel_pipe_update_start/end() instead of of mucking around with crtc->state. v2: The mmio flip stuff is gone Reviewed-by: Maarten Lankhorst <maarten.lankhorst@linux.intel.com> #v1 Signed-off-by: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20170823152226.22938-2-ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com (cherry picked from commit d3a8fb3223a7b2fc50bc818ddbeb780c67420d6d) from v4.15-rc1 Signed-off-by: Tarun Vyas <tarun.vyas@intel.com> BUG=b:70920211, b:109823283 TEST=No *Potential atomic update error* in dmesg with external display connected and browser opened and cursor blinking in address bar for PSR entry-exit TEST=No other regressions on KBL/APL/BYT based devices Conflicts: [Tarun] drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c ["8b5d27b9 drm/i915: Remove intel_flip_work infrastructure" nukes all the legacy flip code. But it is too messy to backport. More importantly, in intel_crtc_finish_commit() we call intel_pipe_update_end() with flip_work struct set to NULL, so retaining the old API doesn't really matters for us and keeps things simpler for the backport.] drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_drv.h [Ctx delta due to other prototype declarations] drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_sprite.c [We don't need "ec1b4ee2 drm/i915: Workaround VLV/CHV DSI scanline counter hardware fail"] Change-Id: Ide1166ed315bea2ff3399fe9789777ee3de0eab8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1135374 Commit-Ready: Nathan Ciobanu <nathan.d.ciobanu@intel.com> Tested-by: Casey G Bowman <casey.g.bowman@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/i915/psr: Move hsw_enable_source after enabling sink. No functional change is expected here since at this point PSR is not allowed to go to any active state. In other words, not really enabled. However let's do in a separated patch so it gets clear on what is change and specially it can helps on bisect case if we figure something has caused changes in behaviour. But this needs to be done before we make the vfunc to enable source to be in parity with VLV implementation. reset: Log the reason for AP resets. Provides a new EC host command 'uptime info' which gathers up some information which may be useful for debugging spurious resets on the AP (was the EC reset recently? Why was the EC reset? If the EC reset the AP, why did it do so?, etc.). Provide ectool support for the same. Example results of `ectool uptimeinfo`: ``` localhost ~ # ectool uptimeinfo EC uptime: 475.368 seconds AP resets since EC boot: 2 Most recent AP reset causes: 315.903: reset: console command 363.507: reset: keyboard warm reboot EC reset flags at last EC boot: reset-pin | sysjump ``` BRANCH=none TEST=Perform some `apreset` commands from the EC console and observe their side-effects via the `ectool uptimeinfo` command on the AP side. Test sequences include no-resets through 5 resets, observing that the ring buffer handling was correct. BUG=b:110788201, b:79529789 Signed-off-by: Jonathan Brandmeyer <jbrandmeyer@chromium.org> Change-Id: I0bf29d69de471c64f905ee8aa070b15b4f34f2ba Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1139028 Commit-Ready: Jonathan Brandmeyer <jbrandmeyer@chromium.org> Tested-by: Jonathan Brandmeyer <jbrandmeyer@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org>

flash_ec: Restore *_ec3po_interp_connect on cleanup() The claim_pty() function forces this control to "off" when the pty is claimed for flashing and relies on the callers to restore it when flashing has completed. But in the case when a flashing fails and we trap into the cleanup() routine, the caller won't restore the setting to "on". Add an explicit restoration for the callers who do so in the cleanup() routine so that EC console works again after flashing fails. BRANCH=None BUG=b:111845859 TEST=make BOARD=cheza && util/flash_ec but make it fail halfway through and then plug and unplug power to board and see EC boot up on console Change-Id: Iacdfd91ac0f9b2dfa15040b12698bc31fa9d4ed2 Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1150729 Reviewed-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com>
